author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Emma Woodhouse was a wealthy, intelligent, and happy young woman. She had a very comfortable and easy life, and for her first twenty-one years in the world, she rarely faced any real problems or stress.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: She was the youngest daughter of a loving but very relaxed father. Since her older sister had gotten married, Emma had been the boss of the house. Her mother had died when she was very young, so she was raised by a kind governess who treated her more like a friend.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Emma and her governess, Miss Taylor, were very close friends. They had lived together for sixteen years, and because Miss Taylor was so gentle, she rarely disciplined Emma. As a result, Emma mostly just did whatever she wanted.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Emma's main problems were that she had too much freedom and thought a bit too highly of herself. These flaws were hidden from her, so she didn't realize they could cause trouble for her in the future.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Emma felt sad for the first time when Miss Taylor got married. On the evening of the wedding, after the guests left and her father fell asleep, Emma sat alone and felt the loss of her companion.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Even though Emma had helped arrange the marriage to Mr. Weston and thought he was a good match, she deeply missed her friend's constant companionship and the comfort of having someone so close to talk to.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Emma worried about being lonely because her father could not provide good conversation. Even though her friend now lived nearby, it wasn't the same as having someone living in the same house.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Her father was old, sickly, and hated change. While he was a nice person that everyone liked, he wasn't energetic or interesting enough to be a good companion for Emma on a daily basis.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Her sister Isabella lived far away in London, so they couldn't visit each other often. Emma knew she would have to endure many long, lonely autumn evenings before the family visited for Christmas.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: There was no one in Highbury who could replace Miss Taylor. Emma tried to be cheerful to keep her father from complaining about the marriage, as he hated change and felt sorry for the bride.
